statement: Differentiate $f(x)=x\\ln x-x$ and hence find $\\int \\ln x\\,dx$.
solution: $f'(x)=\\ln x+1-1=\\ln x$. Therefore an antiderivative of $\\ln x$ is $x\\ln x-x$, so $\\int\\ln x\\,dx=x\\ln x-x+C$.
hints: Use the product rule on $x\\ln x$.
Recognise the derivative gives $\\ln x$ directly.
